claims.text: A ghoul must drink vitae regularly, one blood point a month, to stay a ghoul; a master can make as many as the master has blood to spare.
Ghouls fall into two broad kinds: those Bound to a domitor and independents who have broken free.
A domitor is the vampire who keeps a ghoul; some are close to their ghouls, others treat them as servants or even slaves.

title: Bound Ghouls
summary: Ghouls held by the blood bond.

claims.text: The bond warps a ghoul's feelings: some believe they love their masters enough to die for them.
When a Bound ghoul strikes at another vampire, the victim usually blames the master, who must then punish the ghoul.
A fully Bound ghoul with Willpower 4 finds the bond weakening after eight months with no contact or feeding from the regnant.
A ghoul who feeds from one master finds the bond harder to resist than one who drinks from several vampires.
To keep the bond strong a Bound ghoul must drink from the same master, which keeps such ghouls close to their domitors.
A Bound ghoul keeps more free will and drive than a mortal conditioned with Dominate, which makes such ghouls valuable.
Most vampires frown on independent ghouls as unpredictable and ready to do anything to feed their addiction.
The Camarilla treats every independent ghoul as a future hunter or a Masquerade breach.
They still need vitae every month, so the Blood and freedom are the two needs that drive nearly all of them.
Many know little of vampire society and may not tell a Clan from a bloodline.
Lacking steady access to vitae, they are at high risk of withdrawal, and many hunt vampires for their blood.

title: Ghouls and Age
summary: What happens when old ghouls go without blood.

claims.text: A ghoul kept young by vitae begins to age when the Blood runs out; a 150-year-old Bound ghoul feels the body failing and craves vitae to stop it.
Animal ghouls can be Bound, use a few Disciplines and defend their masters to the death, but cannot speak.
A human-sized or larger animal ghoul holds up to 10 blood points; smaller animals hold far less.
Founded in the 1950s by Gregory Winter, Ginerva Salamanca, Enrico Sagunto and Philip Marshall, it helps ghouls who escaped or were abandoned by their domitors.
It aims to gather enough vitae for its members quietly and to free ghouls from cruel masters.
Newly freed ghouls may stay ghouls or go back to their old lives, and the group finds them new identities.
It works as tight cells and has lately begun to splinter.
The cult claims a near complete copy of the Noddist scripture of Caine, given by the Anathema Ayisha Jocastian.
It sees most modern vampires as sinners against Caine's teaching and wants a return to the First City, with few vampires, many ghouls and willing blood slaves.
Mortals take it for a doomsday cult, and independent ghouls avoid it after clashes with the Unmastered.
Revenant families are lineages of hereditary ghouls; how a family began is left to the Storyteller.
Feuds between families run long, and the rivalry of the Grimaldi and Zantosa is known across the Sabbat.
Once noble warriors of the Tzimisce, the Bratovich fell to begging after their families were jailed for dark arts and died in prison.
Disciplines: Animalism, Fortitude, Vicissitude. They resist frenzy at +2 difficulty and cannot spend Willpower to avoid it, only to end it.
The D'Habi claim a line older than the First City, as warrior-priests of the Baali Methuselah Nergal, worshipped as an underworld god in Mashkan-Shapir.
Disciplines: Presence, Obfuscate, Daimonion. Broken by centuries of servitude, they take +2 difficulty on all Willpower rolls.
The Ducheski were not first related by blood; the family began with a Tzimisce elder named Krevcheski.
Disciplines: Auspex, Dominate, Thaumaturgy. Centuries under the Tremere left them cut off from people, so no Ducheski may have a Social Ability above 2.
The family is said to have begun in sixth century Italy and turned to owning and trading slaves, also selling services such as moving vampires through enemy ground.
Disciplines: Dominate, Obfuscate, Potence. No Enrathi may have Humanity above 3 or Conscience above 2.
Sabbat ghoul candidates are often taken young by Enrathi slavers and trained by the Black Hand.
A wealthy Italian family, the Grimaldi held power before the Tzimisce took them in the late Middle Ages.
Disciplines: Celerity, Dominate, Fortitude. Raised to think the family superior, a Grimaldi must make a Willpower roll at difficulty 7 to hold back scorn when given a chance to boast.
The family grew from a twelfth century split between the Warrior and Sorcerer castes of the Assamites, early in the Ashirra.
Disciplines: Auspex, Celerity, Obfuscate. Careful breeding left every member with the Slow Healing Flaw.
The Obertus began as scholars, monks and clerics serving the Tzimisce Symeon and Gesu in Byzantine Constantinople.
Their costly research into the paranormal may be why the Tzimisce know so much of other supernatural beings.
Disciplines: Auspex, Obfuscate, Vicissitude, with Dominate for Obertus who show the Narov line. Most suffer Obsessive-Compulsive Derangement, and the Narov line Megalomania.
The family descends from the secret police of Ivan the Terrible and serves the Russian Tzimisce as bodyguards, assassins and couriers.
Some now guard the Russian Organizatsiya; the family numbers under a few hundred.
Disciplines: Animalism, Obfuscate, Potence. Each member is haunted by at least one ghost as the Haunted Flaw, and a banished ghost is always replaced.
The matriarchal Rafastio arose along the Po River before Rome and claim, likely wrongly, to be the first revenant family.
Disciplines: Animalism, Auspex, Thaumaturgy. Discipline difficulty is +2 at the new moon, +1 while waxing or waning and -1 at the full moon.
Rafastio blood rejects the Embrace: attempts have always failed, usually killing the revenant and leaving a bloodless corpse that rots at once.
The Giovanni long passed the Rossellini off as a minor family that crossed Claudius Giovanni; in truth Augustus caught them trying to summon an ancient being from the lands of the dead.
Disciplines: Dominate, Fortitude, Necromancy. All have the Deathsight Flaw, with +1 difficulty on Social rolls.
The Ventrue elder Anushin-Rawan made the Aegean island of Yiaros an island-wide Elysium, served by humans living there.
Disciplines: Auspex, Obfuscate, Presence. Near any vampire of the elder's line they serve as if blood bound, to one such vampire at a time, for 10 nights.
Once powerful, the Zantosa withdrew into short-term pleasures and legendary vices, and now court other families and marry into criminal groups such as the Yakuza's Yamaguchi clan.
A Zantosa cannot spend Willpower to resist a supernatural power that tempts toward a new pleasure.

title: Ghoul Disciplines
summary: Which powers ghouls learn and at what cost.

claims.text: Every ghoul learns Potence, whoever the domitor or sponsor is.
A ghoul gets a cost break on the Disciplines of the sponsor's Clan, a revenant on those of the family; independent ghouls find Disciplines hardest to learn and pay more.

title: Revenant Blood
summary: Born ghouls make their own vitae.

claims.text: A revenant's blood pool can hold 10, and unlike a ghoul's it refills naturally over time.

title: Setite Ghouls
summary: Ghouls of the Followers of Set.

claims.text: Setites lean more on their cults than on ghouls and make Bound ghouls mainly to reward cult leaders and keep followers in line.
Their blood carries the Clan weakness, so in time all Setite ghouls grow sensitive to light.
